title: Gazelle on I-5: Exit 759, Louie Road, Shasta Valley
meta: Gazelle on I-5 in California: a tiny town west of the freeway at exit 759 (Louie Road), in Shasta Valley, with rest areas listed to the south and north.
intro: Gazelle is a tiny town of about 95 people, west of I-5 in Shasta Valley, a wide, dry valley of hay fields, cattle and juniper. Its post office took the name Gazelle in 1870. The nearest exit in I-5 Buddy's data is exit 759, Louie Road.

faq.q: What exit is Gazelle on I-5?
faq.a: Gazelle is at exit 759 on I-5, which is Louie Road. The town sits west of the freeway.

faq.q: Is there a rest area near Gazelle on I-5?
faq.a: South of town, Weed Airport Rest Area is at mile 753.1, 3.9 miles from here, and serves both directions. North of town, Randolph E. Collier Rest Area is at mile 785.8, 28.8 miles from here.

faq.q: What is Old Highway 99 near Gazelle?
faq.a: Near exit 755, Old Highway 99 is a two-lane county road between Weed and Yreka. It keeps the same form it had when it was U.S. 99, the main West Coast highway before I-5.

faq.q: What is the landscape around Gazelle?
faq.a: Gazelle is in Shasta Valley, a wide, dry valley in the rain shadow of the Klamath Mountains. It is dotted with hummocks, with hay fields, cattle and juniper.
